card.title: What reset actually moves
card.blurb: `--soft`, `--mixed` and `--hard` move your branch to exactly the same place. Watch where each one leaves the files the undone commit was holding.
hero.title: What reset actually moves
intro.0: You commit something you did not mean to, and the word `reset` starts to sound like a command that deletes your work. It is calmer than that, and it is not one outcome but three. Every reset moves your branch's name back to a commit you name; what changes is where the files from the undone commit end up - still staged, back in the folder, or gone. Watch all three side by side, so you can pick the one you actually meant.
concept.gt-reset.def: Moving your branch's name to another commit, with a choice of what happens to the files you had staged or edited.
step.0.narr: Three commits, and `main` on the newest. That last one is the mistake: it saved `draft.txt` before the file was ready, under the message `oops`. Staging and the working tree are empty, because everything is committed.
step.0.note: `main` sits on the commit you wish you had not made.
step.1.narr: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` moves `main` back one commit, so `oops` is off the line. Now look at staging: `draft.txt` is sitting there, still picked for the next commit. **The snapshot went; the work did not.**
step.1.note: `--soft` - the name moved back, the file stayed staged.
step.2.narr: Run it again with `--mixed` and `main` lands on **exactly the same commit**. One zone is different: `draft.txt` is back in the folder, picked for nothing. You get to choose again what goes into the next commit.
step.2.note: `--mixed` - same move, the file waits in the working tree.
step.3.narr: `--hard` makes the same move once more, and this time it puts `draft.txt` nowhere. Staging empty, folder empty - what that commit was holding is gone. This is the one to read twice before you run it.
step.3.note: `--hard` - same move, the file is thrown away.
step.4.narr: So the branch step is identical in all three, and what you are really choosing is where the files land. That is what makes `--soft` handy: your work is still staged, so one more `git commit` puts it back under the message you meant.
step.4.note: Reset moves a name. The mode decides where your files go.
